evidence.red_flags:
1) 2019 revenue conflict. Quote (2020-04-29) says 2019 'inkomsten' fell 15%+ to €680m. Quote (2021-04-16) says the handelsresultaat rose 'from €464 million' (2019) to €1.4bn+ (2020). €464m gives a smooth cost base (about €256m in 2017, €341m in 2019, €685m in 2020), so it is probably the like-for-like net trading result. €680m may be gross trading income before exchange and clearing costs, or a different line. Treat 2019 net trading revenue as about €464m, with an upside risk to €680m.
2) 2014 base conflict. FD/Quote give 2014 trading revenue as €474m (+17%). Amsterdamtrader says 2015 rose 12% to €587m, which implies €524m for 2014. Possible causes are a restatement or scope change (Cardano deconsolidated in 2015, asset management exited) or a different line item.
3) 2015 profit is €185m (Amsterdamtrader 2016) vs €182.7m (Quote 2017 comparative). 2016 profit has an internal Quote inconsistency: 'ruim €132 miljoen' in the lead vs €128.6m in the body. FD and the 2017 arithmetic support €128.6m.
4) A search snippet of an FD article headed 2022 says IMC 'kept €561 million after costs' in 2022. This is mis-dated: €561m is the 2020 profit, and 2022 was €506m. Another undated FD snippet mentions a 'record year, profit close to €600 million'. It is probably 2020 on a pre-tax or other basis and cannot be attributed.
5) Metric confusion in the press. Quote calls the 2022 figure 'omzet' and the 2025 figure 'handelsomzet'; Bloomberg says 'net trading revenue'. These match IMC's 'net trading revenues' (after direct trading costs, before personnel and opex). Quote's 'winst' is net profit after tax, not trading PnL. Quote 2022's 'variable compensation €125m (2020) / €213m (2021)' looks like cash paid in the year and conflicts with the €678k average 'jaarwedde' for 2020.
6) Headcount discontinuities. The series runs 581 (2014) to 520 average (2015) to 466 (2016), partly from scope changes. Then 774 (end-2020) to more than 1,000 (2021) to 1,121 (2022) to 1,600+ (Dec 2023): a 43% jump in a year when revenue fell 19%, which suggests a change in definition (average FTE vs headcount incl. interns). Revelio Labs (2,491 at Q4 2025; 2,627 at Q1 2026) is about 25-30% above company figures (1,900+; 2,070+). Wikipedia's 1,600 (2024) just repeats the 2024 annual report, so it is not independent.
7) Circular sourcing. All 2024-2025 press figures (Bloomberg, Quote, Substack, Wikipedia, Global Trading) trace to IMC's own annual reports. For 2015-2022, Amsterdamtrader and Quote both draw on the same KvK accounts and FD coverage.
8) Entity traps seen in results and excluded: IMC S.A. (WSE:IMC, Ukrainian agriculture), IM Cannabis, IMC Global (fertilizer), and ZoomInfo's '$360.9m' revenue for an unidentified 'IMC Inc'. IBISWorld's IMC Pacific figure covers the Australian sub-group only.
9) Charity cross-check. IMC donates '2% of total profits'. That implies 'total profits' of about €1.1bn (2022), $1.2bn (2024) and $1.5bn (2025), far above net profit. The definition is unclear (probably pre-bonus or pre-tax), so do not use it as PnL.
10) Currency switch. Reporting moved from EUR (IMC B.V.) to USD (IMC Global Holdings LLC, effective 2024-01-01), with 2023 restated at $1,367m. Do not convert the restated USD figure again.

evidence.red_flags: 1) 2019 conflict: Quote's FY2019 article (2020-04-29) says 'inkomsten ... daalden met ruim 15% tot €680 miljoen'. Quote's FY2020 article (2021-04-16), from the 2020 AR comparatives, says handelsresultaat rose 'van €464 miljoen'. A cost-structure check favours €464m. With €680m, 2019 expenses would be about €560m, which at the reported average €326k per employee implies about 1,000+ staff, against 774 at end-2020. €680m is likely a gross trading-income figure or an error. 2) 2015 growth: Amsterdamtrader/FD says trading income 'rose 12% to €587m', but 2014 was reported at €474m (+24%). Either the 2014 figure was restated or the 12% is wrong. Profit is €185m (FD, Apr 2016) vs €182.7m (Quote's 2016 comparative). 3) 2016 profit: the same Quote article gives both 'ruim €132 miljoen' and €128.6m. 4) Headcount boilerplate: the Dec-21-2023 holding-structure release says 'more than 1600'. That is hard to reconcile with 1,121 for 2022 and with the 2024 AR's '1,600+' after a year of 'significant growth of our organization'. The CMS page may have been edited after publication. 5) Currency and entity break: through FY2023 the reporting entity is IMC B.V. in EUR; from FY2024 it is IMC Global Holdings LLC (US top holdco since 2024-01-01; Dutch tax residence kept) in USD. The 2023 'USD 1,367m' is a translation of €1,264m at about 1.0813, not an independent figure. 6) 'Variable remuneration paid' (€213m in 2021, €125m in 2020) and Quote's 'bonuspot' figures are cash paid for prior-year awards (deferral), not the year's comp expense. Do not use them as personnel cost. 7) The Substack newsletter and Wikipedia simply recycle AR figures (circular). 8) Name traps avoided: IMC S.A. (Ukrainian agri company listed in Warsaw), IMCO, IM Cannabis and IMC Securities LLC. IMC Securities is a US broker-dealer subsidiary whose X-17A-5 gives only a balance sheet (total assets $6.77bn, member's capital $97.6m at FY2025) and is not group PnL. 9) The search-tool summaries sometimes invented framing; I relied only on fetched text or explicitly flagged snippets.

evidence.gaps:
The web search budget for the whole run (200 calls, shared by all agents) was already used up when this agent started, so I ran no web searches. Everything here comes from fetching URLs I could reach directly: imc.com pages; IMC's public CMS (Sanity) API and asset store, where I found the 2023 annual report PDF and a Bloomberg reprint; the 2021 annual report on Publitas; and article URLs for Quote (quotenet.nl) and Amsterdamtrader, taken from local files saved by a sibling IMC agent and re-fetched myself. Per the tool instructions I did not use Wayback Machine snapshots.

Missing by year:
(1) 2017, 2018 and 2019: no headcount found anywhere. Quote gives only average cost per employee (2017 EUR 319k; 2018 at least EUR 426k; 2019 EUR 326k) and says the workforce was growing ('uitdijend personeelsbestand') in 2019. My modeled estimates come from cost per head versus implied personnel cost, taking net trading income less pre-tax profit less about EUR 110-130m of non-personnel opex. evidence.red_flags:
(1) The December 2023 holding-structure release on imc.com now says 'employs more than 1600', but the 2023 annual report (May 2024) says 1,500+. The CMS record was created 2024-10-16 during the site migration, so the boilerplate was probably refreshed. Treat it as anachronistic.

(2) The 2025 annual report headline says 1,900+ IMCers, but emissions per employee (27,075 / 15.3) imply about 1,770. The 2023 and 2024 ratios match their headlines (about 1,501 and about 1,648-1,655). So the 2025 denominator is probably average headcount or FTE. Use about 1,770 as the 2025 average and about 1,915 as year-end.

(3) The 2024 annual report environment table says 'vs 24,611 in 2023' for total CO2, but 24,611 is the restated 2022 baseline. 2023 actual was 22,818, and the 2023 components sum to 22,818. This is a labeling error in IMC's report.

(4) Year-end 2020 is 774 (Quote, from the KvK filing), while year-end 2021 is '1,000+' with only '200+' new starters. Either gross hires well exceeded 200 (the FRIJT Trading acquisition helps) or the 774 is a different basis (FTE or average).

(5) 2019 revenue conflict in Quote: the 2020 article says 'inkomsten' fell more than 15% to EUR 680m, while the 2021 article says 'handelsresultaat' rose from EUR 464m to EUR 1.4bn. These are likely gross vs net trading income. The financial lens should resolve this.

(6) Quote's 'bonuspot' figures (EUR 89m 2016, EUR 125m 2017, EUR 125m and 213m around 2020-21) look like variable pay paid or awarded, including deferrals, not expensed. Do not use them to back out headcount.

(7) Amsterdamtrader is a blog, but its 2014 (581) and 2015 (520 average) figures are corroborated by Quote's independent 'down 10.5%' and EUR 244m / EUR 470k (about 519).

(8) The 2016 figure of 466 continues a decline from 619 (2013) to 581 (2014) to 520 (2015). It is plausible, but it comes from a single press source.

(9) Office pages on imc.com are partly stale: Chicago shows 650+ unchanged since the 2024 annual report, Sydney 300+ vs 350+ in the Modern Slavery Statement, and Mumbai 90+ vs about 120 per Bloomberg in May 2026. Never sum them as a group total.

(10) All headcount figures are self-promotional '+' floors and round numbers; true values are likely 0-5% above the floor.

(11) Entity and currency change: until 2023 the top holding was IMC B.V., consolidated and reporting in EUR. From 2024-01-01 it is IMC Global Holdings LLC ('IMC GH LLC'), reporting in USD; 2023 is restated as USD 1,367m vs EUR 1,264m. The group perimeter is unchanged per the company.

(12) Quote's 2025 '1900 medewerkers' and Wikipedia's '1,600 (2024)' are circular copies of IMC annual reports, not independent confirmation.

(13) An unrelated internal Google Analytics PDF ('data (6).pdf') sits in IMC's public CMS asset store. I ignored it.

evidence.red_flags: 1) Currency and entity break: up to FY2023 IMC B.V. reported in EUR. From FY2024 the top holding is IMC Global Holdings LLC (Delaware, registered as a formeel buitenlandse vennootschap at the Dutch KvK, no. 866138717), reporting in USD. FY2023 is available in both: EUR 1,264m and $1,367m, an implied rate of 1.0815 that matches the 2023 average. Earlier years still need conversion at annual averages (ECB: 2020 about 1.142, 2021 about 1.183, 2022 about 1.053). Trading capital for 2023 converts at an implied 1.125 (EUR 1,557m to $1,751m), which does not match the year-end rate. That suggests a definitional restatement; it does not affect revenue. 2) Headcount inconsistencies: the 2023-12-21 press release says 'more than 1600' employees, while the 2023 annual report (signed 2024-03-14) says '1,500+'. The 2024 report says '1,600+' despite 300 new starters, so the press figure probably includes interns or contractors, or is rounded. Office-level sums run below the headline (about 1,470+ in 2023, about 1,555+ in 2024). All official figures carry '+' and are lower bounds. 3) The website stat '+2070' sits on pages that also show '© 2025' and both '35' and '36' years in trading, so website stats are poorly dated. The CMS update date (2026-07-11) is an upper bound on when 2,070 was set. 4) Metric labels: IMC uses 'net revenue' in key-figure tables and 'net trading revenues' in the text for the same number. It is net of direct trading costs and before the separately reported 'expenses' (personnel, including variable comp, plus other opex), which fits the project's PnL definition. 5) A Wikipedia infobox cites reports.imc.com pages that now 404; its figures match the primary PDF and are corroboration only. 6) The Bloomberg India story (2026-05-08) covers the Indian subsidiary (INR 4.27bn projected 2025 profit, about 120 staff). Do not mistake it for group figures. 7) The project brief's lead ('~EUR 1B+ in 2022') understates the reported figures: 2022 was EUR 1,562m and 2024-2025 were $2,235m and $3,120m. 8) The 2025 annual report PDF was uploaded three times (2026-03-24, -25 and -27), with the 2026-03-27 version linked from the press release. The headline figures are the same in the press summary and the PDF. 9) No 2026 losses, regulatory actions or fund closures were found. That reflects no search capability, not evidence of absence. Known 2025-2026 events: Rob Defares stepped down as CEO in August 2025 (Michael De Lathauwer succeeded him); COO Jan Willem Kohne's departure was announced at the end of 2025; the Aarhus energy-trading office started in Q1 2026; New York expanded into a 35,000+ sq ft office for systematic equities (announced 2026-08-11); 2026 HPC investment was said to exceed 2025's (the research cluster grew 5x in 2025).
evidence.summary: IMC publishes audited group results once a year in an annual report. From FY2024 the reports are in USD under the new top holding, IMC Global Holdings LLC. The primary reports give: FY2025 net trading revenue $3,120m (+40%), expenses $1,800m, net profit $968m, about 1,900+ staff at year-end with FTE up 16% in the year. FY2024: $2,235m (+63%), expenses $1,336m, net profit $686m, 1,600+ staff. FY2023: EUR 1,264m ($1,367m restated), net profit EUR 288m ($312m), 1,500+ staff. From comparatives and older reports: FY2022 EUR 1,562m (profit EUR 506m); FY2021 EUR 1,384m (profit EUR 501m, 1,000+ staff); FY2020 EUR 1,433m (profit EUR 561m). PnL per head is roughly $1.6-1.8m in 2025 on year-end or average headcount, about $1.4m in 2024 and about $0.9m in 2023. No 2026 PnL was found: IMC does not publish interim results, and my search budget was used up before I could look for press or rating-agency interim figures. The latest reliable PnL cutoff is therefore 2025-12-31, and any 2026 YTD value must be an estimate with wide bars. The latest headcount is '2,070+ employees across 10 offices' on imc.com, a value set no later than 2026-07-11 per the site's CMS and still live on 2026-10-08. Regional checks: Sydney 350+ (FYE 2025 statement dated June 2026) and Mumbai about 120 (Bloomberg, May 2026). Recommended bars: about ±1-2% on FY2023-2025 PnL (audited, same definition); about ±5-8% on headcount (lower-bound '+' figures; year-end vs average); FX bars only for EUR years before 2023.

draft.pnl_definition: PnL is IMC's 'net trading revenues' line. The key-results tables call it 'net revenue'; Dutch press calls it 'nettohandelsresultaat' or 'handelsresultaat'. It is trading results net of direct trading costs (understood to be exchange, clearing and brokerage fees) and before personnel and other operating expenses, which IMC reports separately as 'expenses'. Calendar year, group-consolidated: IMC B.V. in EUR through FY2023, IMC Global Holdings LLC in USD from FY2024. This matches the project definition directly, so no adjustment was needed. Net profit attributable to shareholders goes in net_income_usd_m. The '€680m inkomsten' that Quote reported for 2019 is treated as a different, gross line and is not used.
draft.headcount_definition:
Total IMC group employees across all offices. For 2015-2025 the figure is the ANNUAL AVERAGE, because that is the right denominator for a full year's PnL; Dutch statutory accounts also disclose averages.
- 2015 and 2016 are reported averages.
- 2022 (1,121) comes from the jaarrekening and is treated as an average.
- 2020-2025 averages are estimated from consecutive year-end counts and cross-checked against the CO2-per-employee denominators in the annual reports. Year-end values are given in the row notes for anyone who prefers that basis.
- 2017-2019 are modelled from cost per employee.
Company figures are round '+' floors and probably exclude contractors. Interns (80-250 a year) are probably excluded from year-end counts, but this is not stated.
2026 follows the project rule and uses the LATEST KNOWN company figure, not a YTD average: '+2,070 employees', set no later than 2026-07-11. The Jan-Sep 2026 average is probably about 1,990-2,060.
draft.fx_note:
Annual-average EURUSD rates applied to the EUR years: 2015 1.110, 2016 1.107, 2017 1.130, 2018 1.181, 2019 1.120, 2020 1.142, 2021 1.183, 2022 1.053.

2023 uses IMC's own USD restatement in the 2024 annual report and is not converted again: $1,367m net trading revenue (from €1,264m) and $312m net profit (from €288m). The implied rate is 1.0815, against 1.081 in the project table.

FY2024 and FY2025 are reported in USD by IMC Global Holdings LLC, and the 2026 estimate is built in USD. So the approximate 2025 (~1.13) and 2026 (~1.16) rates were never needed.

About ±0.5% of FX uncertainty is folded into the EUR-year error bars. Much of IMC's trading is USD-based (Chicago is the largest office), so the EUR figures were themselves translations; converting them back at average rates approximates the USD economics. The strong dollar in 2022 makes that year look flat in USD ($1,645m vs $1,637m in 2021), even though EUR net trading revenue rose 13%.

caveats: Reporting entity and currency change. Through FY2023 the reporting entity was IMC B.V., in EUR; from FY2024 it is IMC Global Holdings LLC, in USD. IMC says the group perimeter is unchanged. 2015-2022 USD values depend on average-rate translation; 2022 in particular looks flat in USD only because of the strong dollar.

The PnL is IMC's 'net trading revenues', i.e. after direct trading costs and before personnel and other opex, which matches the project definition. For 2015-2019 the figures come from Dutch press quoting the filed accounts ('nettohandelsresultaat'), not from statements I fetched myself. They are assumed to be the same line, but this is not verified.
2018 net trading income was never published. The $709m figure is rebuilt from net profit, cost per employee and opex trends, and its interval runs from about $605m to $835m.

2019 has a metric conflict. Quote reported €680m of 'inkomsten' (2020 article) but €464m of 'handelsresultaat' (2021 article, from the FY2020 report comparatives). €464m is used; the €680m figure is believed to be gross trading income.

There is a 2014-2015 base inconsistency. 2014 was reported at €474m, but 2015's '+12%' implies about €524m, probably reflecting the 2015 scope change (Cardano deconsolidated, asset management wound down). Comparisons across 2014-2016 are not fully like-for-like.

Headcount is reported here as an ANNUAL AVERAGE for 2015-2025, but IMC mostly publishes year-end '+' floors (1,000+, 1,500+, 1,600+, 1,900+). Year-end counts run about 5-9% above the averages in high-growth years (2021, 2023, 2025). PnL per head on a year-end basis would be correspondingly lower; year-end values are in the row notes.
2017-2019 headcounts are modelled from cost per employee and interpolation (±15%). No source gives a headcount for those years.
It is not stated whether IMC headcount figures include interns: 80-250 a year, peaking in summer. The '+2,070' 2026 website figure may include summer interns.
The 2026 PnL is a pure estimate: 9/12 of the FY2025 run-rate. It covers 9 months, so PnL per head for 2026 is not comparable with full years unless annualized (×4/3).

All 2024-2025 press coverage (Bloomberg, Quote, Substack, Wikipedia) traces back to IMC's own annual reports, so it is not independent corroboration. For 2015-2022, Quote, FD and Amsterdamtrader all draw on the same KvK accounts.
Quote's 'bonuspot' and 'variable remuneration paid' figures (€89m, €125m, €213m) are cash paid, including deferred awards, not the year's compensation expense. They were not used to infer headcount.

Third-party workforce data (Revelio Labs: 2,491 at Q4 2025; 2,627 at Q1 2026) is 25-30% above company figures and was rejected. The IBISWorld figure for IMC Pacific is a regional subsidiary figure, not group data.
